items.statement: Company has net cash of INR30 crore and is debt-free
items.quote: Despite these challenges, our balance sheet remains very strong with a debt-free position and net cash of INR30 crore providing ample financial flexibility for future investments.

items.statement: Acquisition funded through internal cash resources, no equity dilution planned
items.quote: No, it will be largely funded through cash only. And we already have sufficient internal resources.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net cash INR270 crores, generated INR25 crores quarterly cash flow
items.quote: we closed Q1 of FY25 with INR270 crores of net cash. And if you see just the Q1 itself on a INR35 crores EBITDA, we generated around INR25 crores of cash flow

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced from 45 days to 38 days on a consolidated basis
items.quote: The net working capital days of the Company which was 45 days as on 31st March '24, they have been reduced to 38 days as on 30th June.

items.statement: Merger eliminates related party transactions between GSPC and GGL, improving GGL profitability and return ratios.
items.quote: This merger eliminates related party transactions between GSPC and GGL and shall contrib ute to further improvement of GGL’s profitability and return ratios going forward

items.statement: GSPC shareholders receive 10 GGL shares for every 305 GSPC shares; GSPL shareholders receive 10 GGL shares for every 13 GSPL shares.
items.quote: The shareholders of GSPC will receive 10 equity shares of GGL for every 305 equity shares of GSPC. Simultaneously, GSPL ‘ India’s 2 nd largest Natural Gas Transmission Company’ merges with GGL. The shareholders of GSPL will receive 10 equity shares of GGL for every 13 equity shares of

items.statement: GGL shareholders receive 1 GTL share for every 3 GGL shares in the demerger of the gas transmission business.
items.quote: Pursuant to such demerger, shareholders of GGL will receive 1 equity share of GTL for every 3 equity shares of GGL.

items.statement: Post-merger GGL share count will be close to 94 crore shares.
items.quote: It will be close to ~94 crore.

items.statement: GSPC has tax losses of approximately INR 7,200 crore that will carry forward to Gujarat Gas for eight years.
items.quote: We have a tax loss of INR7,200 crores, approximately, which will be carried forward to the resulting company i.e. Gujarat gas.

items.statement: GSPC sells 45-50% of its gas trading portfolio to Gujarat Gas on arm's length basis; margin is slightly lower than market.
items.quote: to Gujarat Gas to the extent of 45 to 50% of portfolio. So, that's on a related party basis. That's on an arm's length basis we are selling. So, that's a margin which is a little bit lower than the market

items.statement: GSPC valued at ~INR 21,000 crore; gas trading business at 6.5-7x EBITDA multiple (INR 1,100 crore EBITDA); investments valued at INR 10,600 crore including GSPL at 89%.
items.quote: Yes, I think the valuation which we have taken for GSPC is close to ~INR 21,000 crores. And of that, close to 35% is with respect to the gas trading business. Basically, the valuers have taken a number which is a lower number to the industry average which is there. Basically, if you look at all the previous year, EBITDA number for gas trading is around INR1,100 crores. So, if you compare the numbe

items.statement: GSPL core business valued at INR 3,500-4,000 crore with INR 1,700 crore cash; investments valued at INR 25,000 crore.
items.quote: For the core business the valuation is close to around INR3,500 to INR4,000 crores and they have a cash of around INR1,700 crores. So that's the core valuation and for the investment the valuation is close to INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: GIGL valued at INR 2,000 crore and GITL at INR 181 crore (100% basis); GSPL holds 52% stake.
items.quote: For GIGL it's close to INR 2,000 crores and for GITL it's close to around INR181 crores. That is 100% valuation so basically, we have to come up for the 52% stake of GSPL.

items.statement: No treasury shares created in the transaction; swap ratios as per scheme.
items.quote: No there is no treasury share which is being created . So I think the swap ratio is already mentioned in the scheme itself.

items.statement: Government of Gujarat direct stake in merged Gujarat Gas will be 25.86%; other government entities reclassified as public shareholders
items.quote: So we are just talking about that swap ratio which practically reduces the Government of Gujarat's direct stake to 25.86 but the other holders of the government would be in the category of 74 percentage because they are not the promoters of the company.

items.statement: GSPC shareholding: Governor of Gujarat holds ~55%, GSIL holds ~35%, rest by Gujarat government entities; IDBI, IFC, SBI hold ~6%
items.quote: In GSPC basically 93 % is being held by Government of Gujarat and Government of Gujarat entities. The Governor of Gujarat holds close to 55 %. The GSIL is there the investment of government of Gujarat that holds on close to 35%and rest is held by the government of Gujarat entities. And we have close to 6% percentage being held by IDBI, IFC and SBI.

items.statement: EPS accretive by ~50% for Gujarat Gas shareholders after accounting for 36% equity dilution from merger
items.quote: Yes, it would range between 50% in accretive s would be there in crease , because in the gas trading business is coming into GGL. So practically that EBITDA number of GGL, would be affected

items.statement: GSPC cash balance of ~INR 2,300 crores as of June 2024
items.quote: I think cash position, GSPC, I think we have a, having a cash balance of close to INR2,300 crores as on June ‘24.

items.statement: GSPC LNG Q1 capacity utilization ~29%; FY24 provisional revenue ~INR 235 crores, EBITDA ~INR 137 crores
items.value: 29% utilization, INR 235 cr revenue, INR 137 cr EBITDA
items.quote: I think the last quarter, the capacity utilization was close to 29%. And with respect to the previous year, the provisional numbers in terms of revenues are close to INR235 crores. And they have an EBITDA of close to INR137 crores.

items.statement: Net cash of INR 450 Crores at end of June; raised INR 1,666 Crores gross proceeds from IPO primary issue, net proceeds ~INR 1,600 Crores after issue expenses of INR 60-63 Crores.
items.quote: In June, we had a cash of around INR 450 Crores and we raised around INR 1,666 Crores towards primary issue of capital. This is the gross proceeds. Net proceeds was what we got after adjustment of issue expenses which was close to INR 60 to 63 Crores. So the net what we have got is something around INR 1,600 Crore.

items.quote: The cash �low from operations stood at Rupees 151.8 crores, for �iscal year 2023-24, up 2.9 times compared to Rupees 52 crores generated in the previous year and this is on the back of improved pro�itability and collection

items.statement: Cash and bank balance was Rs 1,082.2 crore as of March 31, 2024, after raising Rs 600 crore via QIP during the year.
items.quote: We continue to have a strong debt free balance sheet and cash, cash position of R upees 1,082.2 crores as of March 31, 2024, with the Company having successfully raised capital of Rupees 600 crores via QIP during the year

items.statement: The company raised Rs 600 crore through a QIP during FY24.
items.quote: with the Company having successfully raised capital of Rupees 600 crores via QIP during the year.

items.statement: Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP is proposed as the new statutory auditor, replacing Walker Chandiok & Co LLP.
items.quote: Resolution number three is - appointment of Deloitte, Haskins Sells, LLP , Chartered Accountants as the Statutory Auditors of the Company and to �ix their remuneration

items.statement: Raised INR200 crores through fresh issue in IPO; proceeds allocated to Athivaram Phase 2 capex, facility upgrades, IT infrastructure, working capital and general corporate purposes.
items.quote: We have raised INR200 crores through fresh issue and net proceeds will be utilized towards the financial and capital expenditure towards settingup of the project in Ath ivaram Phase 2, which is INRS8.5 crores.

items.statement: Company completed a preferential allotment and equity fundraise of Rs 29 crore in FY25.
items.quote: as we all know at FY 25 we did pref. allotment and equity fundraise I think that's also helped us a lot and I think that's going to again, it's going to fuel and it's also going to catalyze our growth over the next few years.

items.statement: Promoters were issued warrants in the fundraise and are yet to convert them as of September 2024.
items.quote: here I think the Promoters are yet to convert the warrants that have been issued to them. Post warrant conversion, there will be further changes to these numbers

items.statement: Of the Rs 29 crore raised, about Rs 3 crore was used for capex, Rs 7 crore for loan repayments, and the rest for inventory increase and working capital including GST input credit.
items.quote: So this is as of June, so you can see about three crores has gone into about three crores gone to Capex, loan repayments about seven crores. We had to increase a little bit of inventory and I think that's helping us now in the metals vertically that's really helping us to scale much faster, helping us to deliver faster to our customers and you can see working capital, increasing working capital GS

items.quote: So this is as of June, so you can see about three crores has gone into about three crores gone to Capex, loan repayments about seven crores. items.statement: Promoters hold warrants issued in the fundraise but have not yet converted them; conversion will further change shareholding pattern.
items.quote: So if you look at 27th March, this is prior to fundraise and if you look at September 2025, that's a post fundraise but here I think the Promoters are yet to convert the warrants that have been issued to them. Post warrant conversion, there will be further changes to these numbers, but this is just a kind of a detail that shows from March to September how the shareholding pattern has changed.
